observations: Photo 0 shows a silver laptop top case with a black keyboard and a trackpad; there is a handwritten signature on the trackpad.
Photo 1 shows the bottom chassis of the same laptop, silver, with four corner screws and a handwritten signature near the center; faint text is visible near the top edge, but not legible.
Photo 2 shows the same top case from a different angle, with the keyboard and trackpad visible; the signature is again visible on the trackpad.
All photos show a single unit: the top case (keyboard, trackpad, and frame) and bottom chassis, which together form a MacBook Pro casing.
No internal components (like logic board, screen, or battery) are visible in any photo.
The seller claims to sell parts including keyboard, battery, mousepad, touch bar, speaker, and chassis — but only the top case and bottom chassis are shown.
The touch bar is not visible in any photo; the trackpad area is flat, suggesting no touch bar is present or it has been removed.
No branding or model identifiers are visible in any photo.

identity.kind: MacBook Pro top and bottom casing

claims.evidence: No visible model identifier or M1 branding in any photo. The design matches pre-M1 MacBook Pro models (e.g., 2016–2019) which had a flat trackpad without a touch bar. M1 models have a different keyboard layout and a touch bar. The absence of a touch bar contradicts the M1 claim.

claims.claim: Parts included: Keyboard, Battery, Mousepad, Touch Bar, Speaker, Chassis
claims.evidence: Only the top case (keyboard, trackpad, frame) and bottom chassis are visible. Battery, speaker, and touch bar are not shown. The trackpad area is flat, indicating no touch bar is present. The seller’s claim of including multiple parts is not supported by the photos.

risks.risk: The item is not an M1 MacBook Pro, but an older model (e.g., 2016–2019), which affects part compatibility and value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the logic board or a close-up of the model number on the bottom chassis or inside the lid.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an older non-M1 model, which is less valuable for parts.

risks.risk: The touch bar is missing or not included, despite being listed as a part.
risks.proof: A close-up of the trackpad area showing the touch bar or its absence.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if touch bar is not included, reducing value.

risks.risk: Battery, speaker, and other internal parts are not included, despite being listed.
risks.proof: Photos of the internal components (battery, speaker, logic board) or a video showing the disassembled parts.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as only casing parts, not as a full set of parts.

risks.risk: The item is damaged or has hidden defects (e.g., cracked frame, non-functional keyboard, or missing screws).
risks.proof: A full 360-degree video or close-up photos of all edges, hinges, and screw holes.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially damaged or incomplete.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model number on the bottom chassis or inside the lid.
A close-up of the trackpad area to confirm presence or absence of the touch bar.
Photos of the internal components (battery, speaker, logic board) to verify included parts.
A video or full set of photos showing all parts and condition, including edges and screw holes.
response.reason: The seller claims to sell an M1 MacBook Pro with multiple parts, but the photos only show the top and bottom casing, and the design suggests a pre-M1 model. The touch bar is not visible, and internal parts are not shown. Without proof of model, included parts, and condition, a reliable price cannot be assigned.
